take_homes: Agent security means giving it less access: ask what it may read, what it may change, and what goes back to a human. The cheapest fix is the door I don't open, and it costs a feature.
A saved audit skill with a policy lens and an agent-risk lens is something a teammate can install and run. That is closer to what I need than clever prompts.
I fixed one risk and the rest are still open. The leftover 'I can't tell' items go to legal or security as narrow questions.

monday.move: List what my pricing-pilot agent can read and change, and pick one door to close. Then run the audit skill on it.
monday.who: Me, then my security/IT contact for the 'I can't tell' rows
monday.when: Monday morning, before the next pricing working group send
monday.stop_condition: One risk has a named mitigation and the open ones are written down with the file or behaviour named
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the skill and context files, so everyone would keep their own copy.

misconception.why: I spent the time on a reusable skill and on deciding what access to remove, not on better prompts. The module never said directly that prompts are not the point.

one_line: Good core hour on what the agent can reach and what you sign for, but the generic 'industry analysts say' slides between the real ones are filler and should go.
